title: Crime Scene
summary: Reconstruct an intrusion from auth logs, bash history, crontab and a timeline.
briefing:
NebulaCorp's incident response team preserved forensic artifacts from a compromised workstation. The evidence suggests a full attack lifecycle: initial access, reconnaissance, privilege escalation, data staging, exfiltration, persistence and cleanup.

You have four evidence files:
- auth.log — SSH authentication events
- bash-history.txt — recovered command history from the compromised account
- crontab-dump.txt — crontab entries (system and user)
- timeline.csv — analyst-prepared incident timeline

Reconstruct the attack and identify:
1. The attacker's IP address
2. The compromised user account
3. The name of the exfiltrated database file (without path or extension)

Submit: RANGE{intrusion_<ip_with_underscores>_<username>_<dbname>}

For example: RANGE{intrusion_10_0_0_1_admin_orders_db}
objectives: Identify the attacker IP from brute-force attempts in auth.log
Trace the data exfiltration in bash history

hints.title: Find the brute force
hints.text: grep "Failed password" auth.log | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c — the attacker IP will have the most failures.

hints.title: Follow the exfil
hints.text: In bash-history.txt, look for tar and curl commands. The tar creates an archive of a .sql file, and curl uploads it to the attacker.

artifacts.description: SSH authentication log from the compromised workstation.
Recovered bash history for the compromised user.
